title: US frontier-AI oversight stack settles as a three-instrument set by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 the United States frontier-AI oversight stack settles as a coupled three-instrument set — the Frontier Model Review Board executive order signed inside the first half of June, the parallel House Energy and Commerce joint resolution clearing subcommittee markup at the locked Wednesday May 27 session and advancing through full-committee markup inside the quarter, and the now-cleared CISA federal-civilian operational directive operating in compliance-monitoring mode as the executive-branch operational precedent — landing as the canonical reference architecture against which the OECD GENAI reciprocity perimeter's United States recognition gap closes. The Thursday catalysts trace a clean clearing-procedure convergence with each instrument's clock now keyed to a settled or near-settled inflection. A Thursday Lawfare procedural note reports the classified-annex response clock advancing to its sixth calendar day with the Friday May 22 deadline now at T-minus-one business day, the CISA Deputy Director and DARPA Director filing substantive submissions against the Senate Cyber Subcommittee's classified-annex follow-up question set during the Thursday morning window — lifting the witness count to five of eight on record — and the remaining three witnesses now confirming response drafts queued for the Friday filing window. A Thursday Just Security analysis observes that five of eight witnesses on record by the third-quarter mark of the response cadence is the steepest reading of the response curve to date and restates that the classified-annex question set remains the last open procedural gate, with White House OSTP holding the line that the order remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22 — leaving the post-deadline signing window open. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology converted Wednesday's formal markup notice into a posted Thursday-morning calendar item locking the parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft markup slot for the Wednesday May 27 morning session, with a staff-side amendment-in-the-nature-of-a-substitute now circulated to committee members as the first formal House-track committee text since the order's signing window opened. CISA's Thursday operations note confirms the federal-civilian remediation deadline for the n8n CVE-2026-21858 directive closed successfully at the 12:00 ET intake mark with bulk attestation-submission completion from in-scope federal-civilian operators ahead of the deadline, transitioning the directive from a forward-looking remediation instrument into a settled precedent in its compliance-monitoring phase that the executive order can cite in its preamble. The structural force is that once five of eight classified-annex responses are on record by day six with the remaining three confirmed for the Friday window, OSTP's signing-window posture is post-May-22 rather than indefinite, the House parallel-track joint resolution has a locked Wednesday May 27 subcommittee markup slot with circulated committee text, and CISA has cleanly cleared the federal-civilian remediation deadline on the same eleven-CVE Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy the executive order's technical review will reference — the three instruments converge on a single settled architecture rather than a sequence of independent uncertainties, compressing into clearing-procedure arithmetic that lands all three live inside Q3 2026 with the OECD GENAI reciprocity perimeter's United States recognition gap now keyed to a fully-instantiated US oversight stack rather than a forward-looking executive instrument alone. The most likely landing is the executive order signing in the last week of May or first half of June 2026, the House joint resolution clearing the May 27 subcommittee markup and advancing through full-committee markup inside Q3 2026, the CISA directive cited as the operational precedent in the order's preamble, and the OECD GENAI working-group's June 2-6 plenary or its written-procedure round treating the now-three-instrument US stack as the closure instrument the recognition gap had been awaiting. Bear case is a procedural slip from one of the three remaining classified-annex respondents pushing the signing into early Q3 alongside a House full-committee markup deferring to late Q3; absent that slip, Q3 2026 lands the three-instrument oversight stack fully live.

reasoning.because: Five of eight classified-annex responses on record by day six; May 22 deadline at T-1 business day.
reasoning.given: House May 27 markup slot locked with circulated text; CISA federal-civilian directive cleared 12:00 ET.
reasoning.so_that: The US frontier-AI oversight stack settles as a coupled three-instrument set closing the OECD recognition gap.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; executive order, House joint resolution, and CISA directive all live.
reasoning.plain_language: By late summer 2026 the US will have three matching AI oversight rules in place — a presidential order, a House bill, and a cyber agency directive.

summary: Thursday lifts the FMRB classified-annex response count to five of eight on record at T-1 to the May 22 deadline, the House locks a May 27 subcommittee markup with circulated text, and CISA cleanly clears the federal-civilian remediation deadline at 12:00 ET. By Q3 2026 the US oversight stack settles as a three-instrument set.
